headline: South Asia: Pakistan conducted strikes at 10 locations in Afghanistan in response to recent drone attacks: info minister
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistan conducted strikes at 10 locations in Afghanistan in response to recent drone attacks: info minister.
- Asia: 8 killed in Russian strikes on Ukraine, maternity clinic damaged.
- Africa: Fighting intensifies in northern Ethiopia as Tigray rebels declare full-blown war.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Army awards Palantir $48.1M to modernize ammo management.
- Military Times, 16 hours ago: Army awards Palantir $48.1M to modernize ammo management.
The tech company has built AI software designed to process data for targeting and decision-making, and now, managing ammo.
- Military Times, 18 hours ago: Army identifies 19th US service member to die amid Iran war.
The U.S. Army identified the 19th U.S. service member to die while deployed in support of the war with Iran.
- Military Times, just now: Nellis Air Force Base says goodbye to last A-10 Thunderbolt II.
After five decades at the Nevada base, airmen saluted its last operational A-10 Warthog as it conducted its final flight Tuesday.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russian attacks destroy Nova Poshta branch and damage sorting depot in Kyiv Oblast.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russian attacks destroy Nova Poshta branch and damage sorting depot in Kyiv Oblast.
Russian strikes on Kyiv Oblast on the night of 23-24 September destroyed Nova Poshta branch No. 6 and damaged one of the company's sorting depots in Kyiv.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Former commander-in-chief Zaluzhnyi: Russia continues to receive imported components, and could strike beyond Ukraine tomorrow.
Ukraine's Ambassador to UK Valerii Zaluzhnyi has warned that imported components for Russian weapons could enable strikes on other countries if not stopped.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russian strike on a farm in Kharkiv Oblast: six killed, twelve injured – photos.
Russian forces struck a vegetable storage facility in Stara Hnylytsia, killing six farm workers and injuring 12, with four wounded hospitalised in a serious condition.
- The Moscow Times, just now: Regions Calling: Russia’s Got a Bear Problem.
At least 19 people have been killed in brown bear attacks across the country since April. What is going on?
Southern Europe - bottom line: Kosovo Marks Banjska Attack Anniversary as Main Suspects Remain Free.
- Balkan Insight, 3 hours ago: Kosovo Marks Banjska Attack Anniversary as Main Suspects Remain Free.
Politicians and relatives paid tribute to Kosovo police officer killed in September 2023 Banjska attack by an armed Serb gang, while the majority of the suspects remain at liberty, most likely in Serbia.
- Balkan Insight, 11 hours ago: Serbian Authorities Ridicule Spyware Attack Allegations Before Elections.
A month away from elections, Serbian authorities show no sign of investigating credible allegations that student protesters, politicians and activists have been targeted with spyware.
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: Le Pen says she won’t leave NATO until Russia’s war in Ukraine ends.
The French presidential front-runner still plans to take Paris out of the military alliance's integrated command, she tells POLITICO.
- Politico Europe, one hour ago: TotalEnergies refused rescue aid during deadly Mozambique attack, inquest hears.
Sworn testimony comes as energy giant faces two criminal complaints in France over its Mozambican operations.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Fighting intensifies in northern Ethiopia as Tigray rebels declare full-blown war.
- Africanews, 2 hours ago: Fighting intensifies in northern Ethiopia as Tigray rebels declare full-blown war.
Ethiopia’s army says its forces have killed 272 Tigrayan fighters and wounded 260 during a counter-offensive in Amhara. The press says the figures could not be independently verified.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 3 hours ago: Ethiopia: Ethiopia - Renewed Tigray Fighting Shows Need to Protect Civilians.
[HRW] Nairobi -- Fighting in Ethiopia's northern Tigray, Amhara, and Afar regions erupted on September 22, 2026, between the Ethiopian military and forces aligned with the Tigrayan People's Liberation Front, Tigray's main political party. This follows reported clashes and airstrikes in Tigray since August, including in Tigray's regional capital, Mekelle.
- Africanews, 7 hours ago: Tigray tensions rise as regional forces seize Mekelle airport.
The developments follow a series of reported drone strikes in Tigray. Regional authorities say at least 14 people were killed and 22 injured in a strike on the town of Alamata on Tuesday, with the mayor accusing federal forces of targeting schools.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 4 hours ago: Ethiopia: Attack By Rebel Group Raises Fear of Renewed War in Ethiopia.
[Premium Times] Months of rising tension in Ethiopia have now escalated into renewed armed clashes in the northern Tigray region, raising concerns that the country could slide back into a civil war.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Israel ready to resume strikes on Iran as regime aims to rebuild nuclear program - report.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Israel ready to resume strikes on Iran as regime aims to rebuild nuclear program - report.
"We will move to strike nuclear facilities and any site belonging to them again if Tehran crosses any of the red lines, whether with or without the participation of the US," an Israeli official said.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Deadly attack on Indian cargo ship off coast of Oman.
A crew member was killed in an attack on an Indian cargo vessel off the coast of Oman.
- Jerusalem Post, 5 hours ago: Hamas 'ready' to move forward with Board of Peace ceasefire roadmap for Gaza, terror group says.
Hamas spokesperson Hazem Qassem accused Israel of escalating aggression against Gazans, claiming that the Board of Peace and its director-general were unable to stop the Israeli government.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Saudi-led coalition says shot down 6 ballistic missiles launched by Houthis.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 2 hours ago: Angola: Angolan Businessman Dinstinguished With Forbes Best of Africa Prize.
[ANGOP] New York -- Angolan businessman Edson dos Santos was distinguished on Tuesday (22), in New York (USA), with the Forbes Best of Africa Prize, at the Forbes Africa Day Award ceremony.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 6 hours ago: Namibia: Kahungu Cruises Towards Another Term.
[Namibian] Swapo Party Women's Council (SPWC) secretary Fransina Kahungu is set to return for another five-year term after being nominated unopposed to lead the women's wing at its upcoming ninth congress.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 7 hours ago: Malawi: World Bank Warns Malawi's Mining Potential Hinges On Solving Electricity Crisis.
[Nyasa Times] Malawi's drive to build a mining industry around critical minerals is being held back by a chronic electricity shortage, according to a new World Bank report that warns the country's mineral wealth could remain largely untapped without urgent power sector reform.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan conducted strikes at 10 locations in Afghanistan in response to recent drone attacks: info minister.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: Pakistan conducted strikes at 10 locations in Afghanistan in response to recent drone attacks: info minister.
Pakistan has conducted precision aerial and drone strikes in 10 locations across Afghanistan in retaliation for drones launched from the neighbouring country a day earlier, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said in the early hours of Thursday. “In exercise of its sovereign right to self-defence, Pakistan conducted precision aerial and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan used for launching and storing these drones,” Tarar wrote in a post on social media platform X.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: 8 terrorists killed in KP's North Waziristan: security sources.
Security forces killed eight terrorists in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan during an intelligence-based operation (IBO), security sources said on Thursday. The sources said the terrorists belonged to Fitna al Khawarij — a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). The hideouts used by the terrorists were also completely destroyed during the operation, according to security sources.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: PM Shehbaz meets Iranian President Pezeshkian on UNGA sidelines.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Thursday on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York. In a post on the social media platform X, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said the meeting had begun, adding that the two would discuss Pakistan-Iran relations and the situation in the region.

A Croatian court has approved the extradition of a Ukrainian man who is wanted in Germany in connection with the 2022 undersea explosions that damaged the Nord Stream gas pipelines, state media said on Thursday. The report from HRT Television quoted the suspect’s lawyer Ljubo Pavaskovic as saying that he will appeal the September 18 ruling. It was not immediately clear when the man could be handed over to Germany. He was arrested on a European warrant in the northern Croatian town of Pula in...

- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Wrestler Attacked With Chilli Powder, Beaten To Death With Bamboo Sticks In UP.
According to police, wrestler Brahmanand Yadav was travelling on his motorcycle towards Gidhini market on Tuesday when the accused allegedly intercepted him near Rakesh's house.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Did AI-‘kill chain’ lead to deadly Iran school strike? What report claims.
A devastating missile strike by the US on a school in Minab, Iran, has led to the tragic loss of over 150 lives, including 123 innocent children. Investigations uncovered serious issues in the military’s targeting tactics, pointing to outdated intelligence and a lack of comprehensive civilian harm evaluations. The AI-powered Maven Smart System was crucial in target assessments.
- NDTV - Top Stories, Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Trump-Xi Jinping LIVE Updates: Trump, Xi To Talk Trade, AI, Iran War At US-China Bilateral Meet.
Trump-Xi Jinping LIVE Updates: Trade tariffs, technology, AI, military ties, conflicts in Middle East, the Russia-Ukraine war, the arms race in space and US arms sales to Taiwan are expected to figure in talks between Xi and Trump.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: How Iran’s rowers trained through war to win multiple Asian Games gold medals.
Iran’s rowing team delivered a historic six-medal haul at the Asian Games in Nagoya after months of preparation disrupted by the Israel-Iran conflict. With athletes forced to train separately and indoors, Fatemeh Mojallal, Kimia Zarei and Zeinab Norouzi led the breakthrough, securing Iran’s first women’s rowing golds at the Games while the team added further silver and bronze medals.

A government database has been hacked for the first time by a rogue OpenAI agent, which infiltrated part of the Australian healthcare scheme in June. OpenAI became aware of the hack in August, but only informed the government in September. Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese, has expressed his ‘extreme concern’ about the hack, which raises serious AI security concerns for governments around the world. The NSW premier has urged the world to listen to the warnings of artificial intelligence bosses about the technology's potential dangers, after a state dataset found it could be vulnerable to exploitation.
